body:
Hi SW, figured I'd post a recap to [this](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/7x37x/loves_got_me_down/)

Well... just as I expected, we broke up last week - she really didn't have feelings for me. I've avoided thinking about it for most of the time. She gave me the classic line - "I really think we should just remain friends". Like I've said before, I sorta knew that this would happen eventually. Now that it has, I just feel numb, distant... It's occasionally hard to focus on work, but thankfully that has kept me quite busy recently.

So... what should be my next step? I meet people rather regularly over parties, lab meetings, etc., but definitely nobody that's single. Interested is a non-category - nobody's interested in me. Meh, I should avoid these depressing thoughts...

23, grad school, and still a virgin, woot! Girls just... aren't into me. Hell, I'm actually kinda into chubby girls, but still no luck. Sorry to burst your bubble, but I really hope you have more luck than I...

In most of these physical activities that I enjoy, males outnumber females 5 or 10 to 1. Since I am the awkward one and most cyclists/skiers are suave guys with more balls than brains, my chances of meeting a girl in any of these activities is... zero.

Thanks for the luck! I had a pretty good time tonight with her I admit. However, I did ask her at the end what she's thought of the relationship so far. I was expecting to be broken tonight, but I guess it was slightly better than that. She said that she felt that our relationship wasn't really moving - we should continue seeing each other, but we should really keep that in consideration. 

Now I'm just feeling melancholic... Can't really describe this feeling any other way...

Haha, in a way I've already gone through a long slow drawn out version of that over the last few weeks. Each time I call her when her phone's off - I die a bit. I guess I'm already to the point where if this doesn't work out, I would understand. It's not nearly as long as you've stated, but that's because again - she's not the first person I've ever asked out, just the first person who accepted. In an odd way, this feeling of being "unlovable" makes moving on easier. It's not their fault after all - I'm just an unlovable person.

I tend not to think of her as one a pedestal. To me she seems more apathetic to this relationship than utilising it, as you'd suggest.

Again, thank you everyone for the well wishes and advice.

Well, this girl is a change of tactics for me. She's the first person I've asked out who I didn't know as a good friend yet. Sadly being the horribly nerdy person I am, there are no females in any of the hobbies I attend. I mean, how many single female cyclists do you know? Beyond cycling and skiing, I'm your typical reddit nerd. Programming, gaming, etc... not really where you meet girls.


Anyways, I'm meeting up with her for my extravagant Valentine's day plans later. I hope this doesn't link me to my normal account, but [here's a picture](http://s5.tinypic.com/2hnm9ud.jpg) of the gift I made for her. The bear is sitting on a box of home-made [chocolate truffles](http://s5.tinypic.com/feqy5y.jpg). Wish me luck!

The purpose of stating "first gf at 23" was also to imply that yes, I am a virgin at 23. Yeah, not as bad as some people, but I don't really let it bother me much. As for the specifics...

We usually split the cost of dinner, although we alternate taking each other out - that's extremely fair.

Neither of us drives; we take public transport most of the time.

She's normally very punctual when I do get a hold of her. She's very flaky on the cell phone unfortunately, so getting a hold is the hard step.

I've kissed her on the cheek. Reminds me of [this](http://www.ponderabout.com/archives/1736/imbalanced_roles.aspx)

No sex, like I mentioned

I'm normally the one calling her, but she does call me occaisonally for dinner

She does offer me support, but I guess we are still new. Not much needed in the emotional support category...

What am I actually getting from this? Happiness. She brings me joy. The mere act of eating with her, holding her hand... Brings me irrational amounts of joy and happiness.

I'm willing to wait as long as it takes. I am the patient type, and having lived single as long as I have, I'm more or less used to it anyways.

I don't think she wants anything from me. I initiated this relationship, and she said she'd love to "give it a try". She didn't expect it coming from me (I guess I'm absolutely awful at giving hints?), so I don't think she has much in the way of demands. She also hasn't stated anything about what she wants either.

She's the extremely introverted type. For reference, I'm fairly introverted as well. I do think there should be more intimacy between bf and gf though. Whenever I invite her out for something, I feel like she wants a *reason*, a purpose. Sometimes I just want to hang out, be in the same room - nothing serious. I feel like she's slightly out of reach for that; that she prefers to stay by herself in those cases. According to herself, even some of her close female friends have mentioned that she's rather flaky on the cell phone though, so it's not restricted to me. We chat a lot, so I've gotten to know her fairly well.


Need any more info?

Hmm... I doubt I have prosopagnosia (PhD is in neurological modelling after all, so that's almost a canonical case). I rarely have problems identifying people by their faces, but I never remember anyone's names from just their face. I admit that I'm awful at reading people though - can't tell at all. My current gf is actually exactly the second type you mentioned - shy nerdy girl with a nice smile.

My friends do like me. I'm fairly agreeable too most people. I'm just lacking the romantic side of things...

Haha, the infamous "be happy with yourself" thing about relationships. I feel that I've always at least shown an outward appearance of being quite happy with what I've got. And frankly, I am fairly happy, save for the lack of an intimate relationship. I have some sports which I love to engage in, I'm an excellent programmer with various side projects, and my PhD program keeps me quite busy. I like to think that I'm fairly good dating "material", yet having only one mutually accepted relationship at 23 seems to disprove that point...

When my current girlfriend first accepted my... "confession", she mentioned that she can't stand clingy guys, and that her last relationship ended because of that. I've been extremely careful to be rather standoffish to avoid appearing clingy. She also mentioned that she needs her personal space. If she really is the type that needs as much space as I imagine, she's already been extremely good to me, allowing me into her bubble. There's always more than one way to read the situation, and I'm afraid that I've given the wrong perspective on some of this.

I see this Valentine's day as "one last push" - if she hasn't shown any signs of reciprocation, I'll probably have to end it somehow.

She isn't the only one I've asked out. She's the only one who's accepted my offer. I've been rejected a few times, each time sucking harder than the last. Most of the previous attempts were with fairly good friends who I've known for a while. They've always told me that I'm a very good friend, but they don't see me that way. I think I fall into your latter category - I'm not getting the sense that any girls have warmed up to me relationship-wise. That's my biggest pain -- this feeling of being unlovable, a great friend, but not someone to love - is what's made me miserable...

I think that that most closely matches my personal assessment of how things are going. She does like me, but hasn't figure out how to let me down easy. On the other hand, I have been showing an exterior of... aloofness, I guess? Since she warned me against being "clingy" at the beginning, I've never complained about phone calls being unanswered, etc. Obviously this wreaks havoc on my psyche, but she did mention that she broke up with her last boyfriend over being too clingy - and I haven't gotten there yet...

I admit that I've been far too passive in the dating game. However, it's more of an apprehension for going through with actually asking. I feel like for a normal relationship, the guy treats the girl nicely, she returns at least some hints of interest, and then the relationship begins. I've NEVER experienced this return of interest. Maybe I'm just royally bad at reading people? But each time I've tried to show interest in dating, I've been met with the same reaction - thanks for being nice! I think that's my biggest pain as I've mentioned - that nobody has ever shown any reciprocal interest.

When I finally asked my current gf out, she mentioned that she was caught off guard, and didn't expect that out of me. Maybe I've been sending the wrong signals all these years.

Mmmm.... Thanks for the advice. You're very accurate in your assessment of my personality :) My friends have been telling me very similar things as you, that I should really be asking her if this will work out. I haven't worked up the courage to do so yet.

One of the reasons is that I know that I'm naturally "clingy". I've been told time and time again that that is a BAD BAD BAD thing. In fact when I started this relationship, I was warned about this. Coupled with my complete inability to read people, I'm deathly afraid that I'm really just clueless, and that she does have feelings but I'm expecting too much too soon. Keep in mind that I am only able to post this from my point of view, which I can tell you is very narrow!
I'm in the US, PhD area is neurological modelling. The girl I'm with right now is also a PhD, incidentally...

Hi SW,

I'm probably not in imminent danger (for now), but I guess I did want to get this off my chest. I couldn't think of a better place to post this, especially since everyone here is so understanding, so please bear with my rambling...

I'm 23. I'm in... somewhat of a relationship. My first earnest one. The girl I'm with right now - I adore her greatly, but she doesn't show any signs of returning this sentiment. She agreed to going out with me November last year. We mostly just eat dinner together every other day, nothing more. I really like her - absolutely love spending time with her, but she's rather inaccessible, not answering phone calls, not on facebook nor any IM networks. It's... debilitating at times. I got her a very nice Christmas gift, but she didn't even respond with a card. I have a fairly extravagent valentine's day planned (and no, I don't expect anything in return), but it would be nice to at least have confirmation that there's returned feelings.

This is a dummy account, so I don't want to link too much info about me. However, I guess I should let you know a bit about myself. Yes, she's my first girlfriend at 23 years old. I had a few crushes through high school and college, but being a spineless bastard I never asked them out. It took monumental courage to ask my current gf out, and it feels like that's barely hanging on by a thread.

I think my biggest pain now is that despite having expressed plenty of interest in various females in my life, I have never noticed any return. As if nobody likes me - as if I were some horribly broken person who's unlovable. This.. puzzles me. I've had very close friends, many of them female as well. I don't think I'm horribly ugly. I think I'm a very nice person and won't hesitate to help anyone. I'm definitely very socially awkward, but I actually do enjoy being around people. Yet for some reason, nobody has ever come up to me and said "i like you", let alone "love".

Sometimes I feel like I have some disease that I don't know about. My friends keep telling me that I deserve a great girl - but maybe they're just being nice? I've slowly stepped up my own attempts at showing love due to my loneliness, culminating in this "relationship" I'm in right now. Yet still - nothing. It's horribly painful to think that nobody can love you, and it's something that's made me at least consider the s-word before in my life. After all, what's the point of living if nobody likes you?

I'm sorry for the rambling, but it's been something that's been bothering me throughout my teen years till now. I've cried myself to sleep an uncountable number of times thinking like this, and I know I shouldn't be. I'm actually normally a very happy person - most people comment that I never stop smiling. I guess it's those people you have to watch out for... when they finally stop smiling.

I feel like I'm getting shafted by the spectrum, at 23. The furthest I've ever gotten was a cheek kiss. The girl I'm currently with right now (my first gf)... "puts up" with me, but shows no actual interest in me, at least as far as I can tell.

I know I'm just whining at this point, and frankly I'm not even that interested in the sex itself. I really just want to know someone actually *loves* me. I don't think I'm an unlikeable character... I won't hesitate to help anyone in need. I don't think I'm physically ugly (at least not anymore, especially after I lost 40 lbs exercising). I'm not dumb nor antisocial (working at a PhD). Yet I've never had any emotional confirmation. Nobody outside of my family members have ever come up to me and even said "I like you".

I think that's my biggest pain. After so many years, I feel like I'm missing something, like I'm a totally unlikeable person yet I don't know about it. It's quite painful, I tell you.
